subject.title: [Bug]: Large SQLite transcript cleanup blocks the gateway event loop

question: Should OpenClaw accept the linked Worker-based archive phase as the immediate responsiveness fix while leaving bounded-memory extraction and reclamation-tail work in this issue?
rationale: The report and PR deliberately split a storage-concurrency change into phases; accepting the first phase determines the repository’s near-term performance and durability boundary rather than merely resolving a mechanical defect.

options.title: Land the bounded Worker phase
options.body: Review and land the linked PR if its snapshot, durability, and upgrade behavior are accepted, then keep this issue for measured residual memory and reclamation work.

options.title: Require a different complete design first
options.body: Keep the issue and PR open until maintainers choose a streaming or reclamation design that addresses the remaining memory and tail-stall scope together.

recommendation.title: Land the bounded Worker phase
recommendation.body: Review and land the linked PR if its snapshot, durability, and upgrade behavior are accepted, then keep this issue for measured residual memory and reclamation work.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the adjacent archive durability path and identified this follow-up boundary.
